H5329: properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent
H1121: a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense (of literal and figurative relationship, including grandson, subject, nation, quality or condition, etc., (like father or brother), etc.)
H7141: Korach, the name of two Edomites and three Israelites
H430: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
H241: broadness. i.e. (concrete) the ear (from its form in man)
H8085: to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)
H1: father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application
H5608: properly, to score with a mark as a tally or record, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe, and also to enumerate; intensively, to recount, i.e. celebrate
H6466: to do or make (systematically and habitually), especially to practise
H3117: a day (as the warm hours), whether literal (from sunrise to sunset, or from one sunset to the next), or figurative (a space of time defined by an associated term), (often used adverb)
H6924: the front, of place (absolutely, the fore part, relatively the East) or time (antiquity); often used adverbially (before, anciently, eastward)
H859: thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you
H3027: a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.),
H1471: a foreign nation; hence, a Gentile; also (figuratively) a troop of animals, or a flight of locusts
H3423: to occupy (by driving out previous tenants, and possessing in their place); by implication, to seize, to rob, to inherit; also to expel, to impoverish, to ruin
H5193: properly, to strike in, i.e. fix; specifically, to plant (literally or figuratively)
H7489: properly, to spoil (literally, by breaking to pieces); figuratively, to make (or be) good fornothing, i.e. bad (physically, socially or morally)
H7971: to send away, for, or out (in a great variety of applications)
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H2719: drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement
H776: the earth (at large, or partitively a land)
H2220: the arm (as stretched out), or (of animals) the foreleg; figuratively, force
H3467: properly, to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively, to free or succor
H3225: the right hand or side (leg, eye) of a person or other object (as the stronger and more dexterous); locally, the south
H216: illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.)
H6440: the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.)
H7521: to be pleased with; specifically, to satisfy adebt
H1931: he (she or it); only expressed when emphatic or without a verb; also (intensively) self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are
H3444: something saved, i.e. (abstractly) deliverance; hence, aid, victory, prosperity

H5055: to butt with the horns; figuratively, to war against
H8034: an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character
H6965: to rise (in various applications, literal, figurative, intensive and causative)
H7198: a bow, forshooting (hence, figuratively, strength) or the iris
H982: figuratively, to trust, be confident or sure
H954: properly, to pale, i.e. by implication to be ashamed; also (by implication) to be disappointed or delayed
H1984: to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make ashow, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively, to celebrate; also to stultify
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H5769: properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always
H3034: physically, to throw (a stone, an arrow) at or away; especially to revere or worship (with extended hands); intensively, to bemoan (by wringing the hands)
H637: meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though
H3637: properly, to wound; but only figuratively, to taunt or insult
H3318: to go (causatively, bring) out, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively, direct and proxim.
H6635: a mass of persons (or figuratively, things), especially reg. organized forwar (an army); by implication, a campaign, literally or figuratively (specifically, hardship, worship)
H7725: to turn back (hence, away) transitively or intransitively, literally or figuratively (not necessarily with the idea of return to the starting point); generally to retreat; often adverbial, again
H268: the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West
H4480: properly, a part of; hence (prepositionally), from or out of in many senses
H5414: to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.)
H6629: a collective name for a flock (of sheep or goats); also figuratively (of men)
H3978: an eatable (includ. provender, flesh and fruit)
H2219: to toss about; by implication, to diffuse, winnow
H4376: to sell, literally (as merchandise, a daughter in marriage, into slavery), or figuratively (to surrender)
H5971: a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock
H7760: to put (used in a great variety of applications, literal, figurative, inferentially, and elliptically)
H7934: a resident; by extension, a fellow-citizen
H5439: (as noun) a circle, neighbour, or environs; but chiefly (as adverb, with or without preposition) around
H4912: properly, a pithy maxim, usually of metaphorical nature; hence, a simile (as an adage, poem, discourse)
H4493: a nodding or toss (of the head in derision)
H7218: the head (as most easily shaken), whether literal or figurative (in many applications, of place, time, rank, itc.)
H5048: a front, i.e. part opposite; specifically a counterpart, or mate; usually (adverbial, especially with preposition) over against or before
H1322: shame (the feeling and the condition, as well as its cause); by implication (specifically) an idol

H2778: to pull off, i.e. (by implication) to expose (as by stripping); specifically, to betroth (as if a surrender); figuratively, to carp at, i.e. defame; to spend the winter
H5358: to grudge, i.e. avenge or punish
H935: to go or come (in a wide variety of applications)
H7911: to mislay, i.e. to be oblivious of, from want of memory or attention
H8266: to cheat, i.e. be untrue (usually in words)
H1285: a compact (because made by passing between pieces of flesh)
H5472: properly, to flinch, i.e. (by implication) to go back, literally (to retreat) or figuratively (to apostatize)
H3820: the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything
H5186: to stretch or spread out; by implication, to bend away (including moral deflection); used in a great variety of application
H734: a well-trodden road (literally or figuratively); also a caravan
H4725: properly, a standing, i.e. a spot; but used widely of a locality (general or specific); also (figuratively) of a condition (of body or mind)
H8577: a marine or land monster, i.e. sea-serpent or jackal
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H6757: shade of death, i.e. the grave (figuratively, calamity)
H518: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!; interrogative, whether?; or conditional, if, although; also Oh that!, when; hence, as a negative, not

H410: strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity)
H2114: to turn aside (especially for lodging); hence to be aforeigner, strange, profane; specifically (active participle) to commit adultery
H2713: properly, to penetrate; hence, to examine intimately
H3045: to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)
H2803: properly, to plait or interpenetrate, i.e. (literally) to weave or (generally) to fabricate; figuratively, to plot or contrive (usually in a malicious sense); hence (from the mental effort) to think, regard, value, compute
H2878: {properly, something slaughtered; hence, a beast (or meat, as butchered); abstractly butchery (or concretely, a place of slaughter)}
H4100: properly, interrogative what? (including how? why? when?); but also exclamation, what! (including how!), or indefinitely what (including whatever, and even relatively, that which); often used with prefixes in various adverbial or conjunctive senses

H136: the Lord (used as a proper name of God only)
H408: not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing
H5331: properly, a goal, i.e. the bright object at adistance travelled towards; hence (figuratively), splendor, or (subjectively) truthfulness, or (objectively) confidence; but usually (adverbially), continually (i.e. to the most distant point of view)
H5641: to hide (by covering), literally or figuratively
H6083: dust (as powdered or gray); hence, clay, earth, mud
H5315: properly, a breathing creature, i.e. animal of (abstractly) vitality; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental)
H1692: properly, to impinge, i.e. cling or adhere; figuratively, to catch by pursuit
H990: the belly, especially the womb; also the bosom or body of anything
H6299: to sever, i.e. ransom; gener. to release, preserve
H4616: properly, heed, i.e. purpose; used only adverbially, on account of (as a motive or an aim), teleologically, in order that
H2617: kindness; by implication (towards God) piety; rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty
